findings.title: gbg scan's DEAD/exit-code semantics changed for the population==0-with-hits case
findings.before:
if r.population == 0 && r.exempted == 0
    println(io, "  DEAD  ", rpad(r.id, 30), " measured nothing", ...)
    code = 2
elseif !isempty(r.hits)
    ...
findings.after:
if r.population == 0 && r.exempted == 0 && isempty(r.hits)
    println(io, "  DEAD  ", rpad(r.id, 30), " measured nothing", ...)
    code = 2
elseif !isempty(r.hits)
    ...
findings.why_it_matters: For any hard-tier scan able to report population==0 while still holding hits (SCAN.FIELD_DOCS could: at base, `checked` — the population counter — was only incremented in the branch that runs AFTER a NOLIST hit is pushed, so a corpus whose sole finding was a NOLIST case reported population 0 with hits non-empty), `gbg scan docs` previously printed `DEAD ... measured nothing` and returned exit 2 (cannot evaluate) while silently DROPPING the hit from the report entirely — no FAIL line, no hit text, anywhere. After this diff the same input prints `FAIL ... N hit(s)` with the hit shown and returns exit 1. A CI pipeline or a script keyed on exit code 2 vs 1 for this scan, or a human reading the report for this input, gets a different, now-correct, answer than before. The fix is real and narrowly scoped, but it does silently change a computed result (exit code and printed content) for an input that previously produced clean-looking (if wrong) output, and nothing in this diff's visible surface (no CHANGELOG.md entry is part of this changeset) announces it.
findings.description: Both of Scan.jl's report() loops (hard and triage) and Rounds.jl's prepare() mirror of the same guard now require `isempty(r.hits)` before classifying a scan DEAD; previously a scan whose population counter under-counted (as SCAN.FIELD_DOCS's did, fixed in the same diff) could have real hits silently swallowed under a DEAD/exit-2 verdict instead of being reported and exit 1. The fix is correct, internally consistent, and traceable to a real root-cause bug in field_docs.jl's population counter, but it is a genuine, unannounced change to `gbg scan`'s exit-code and report-content contract for that edge case.
findings.evidence:
src/Scan.jl base: `if r.population == 0 && r.exempted == 0
    println(io, "  DEAD  ", ...)
    code = 2
elseif !isempty(r.hits)`; head: `if r.population == 0 && r.exempted == 0 && isempty(r.hits)`. src/Scans/field_docs.jl base had `checked += 1` AFTER the `documented === nothing` early-continue (so a NOLIST-only run left `checked == 0`); head moves it before, with the comment '# NOLIST hit with population 0 reads as a DEAD scan'.
